- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-package/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run

The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 546d7d5deb69185f23e333807a2b6a78d54410d4 && git checkout 546d7d5deb69185f23e333807a2b6a78d54410d4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e a263c0885f1376f32d866f2c106b88bf90187608 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e && git merge --no-ff a263c0885f1376f32d866f2c106b88bf90187608

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e
```

</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8a88901be1c317e2e078e6d29f21efcae5b9485e` → pass the list as

### ① Derived judgments

1. **What `protocol.installPackage` now refuses, and the declaration each refusal follows from — all RIGHT.** The gate is `PackageInstallManifestSchema.safeParse(manifest)` (protocol.ts 31429), the schema `POST /api/v1/packages` parses on both body forms (`PackageInstallRequestSchema.manifest` and the bare branch of `PackageInstallBodySchema`, package-api.zod.ts 230, 289, 517). It is `ManifestSchema.extend({ scope: z.enum(['project']) })`, so the new refusals are exactly: `type` outside the `ManifestSchema` enum (`plugin`, `ui`, `driver`, `server`, `app`, `theme`, `agent`, `objectql`, `module`, `gateway`, `adapter`; `application` is not a member and `type` has no default); a missing `type` or `name` (both required, manifest.zod.ts); `scope` other than `project` (`environment`, and the platform scopes `cloud` / `system`, refused with `packageInstallScopeRefusal`'s own sentence); any undeclared top-level key (`ManifestSchema` is a `strictObject` and `.extend()` keeps the close — `pages`, `icon`); and, by the same declaration, an explicit `namespace` or `version` the field regexes refuse, a tombstoned key, and a nested-shape violation inside a declared block. Each refusal throws `{ statusCode: 400 }`, which `resolveThrownHttpError` resolves to `{ status: 400, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' }` (`standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(400)`), the envelope the door's `deps.error(msg, 400)` answers. No value is decided in this file: no enum copy, no hand-written rule; the message is `Invalid package manifest — manifest.KEYPATH: ISSUE` with the declaration's own issue text.

2. **Door versus primitive — RIGHT, with one pre-existing asymmetry named.** The door (packages.ts 1227–1366) parses the raw body through `PackageInstallBodySchema` after its own `id` and `version` legs, then hands `manifest = body.manifest || body` — the manifest as SENT, not the parsed copy — to `protocolSvc.installPackage({ manifest, settings })` (1423). The primitive re-parses that same object through the same sub-schema, so nothing the door admits is refused by the primitive. In the other direction the primitive admits one thing the door refuses: a manifest with no `version`, because the #2532 default (`version = '0.1.0'`, protocol.ts 31398) runs before the parse. That is deliberate and pre-existing (the primitive admitted it before this diff too), the stored row is declaration-conformant after the default, the door's own version leg is untouched, and the changeset states it under Unchanged — so it is not a widening and not this card's target (the card's measured defect is the in-process `type` / `scope` rows). `namespace`: the parse runs before the derivation; the declaration's `namespace` is optional, so an explicit value is judged and the derived one is not — and `deriveNamespaceFromPackageId` answers `null` unless `NAMESPACE_RE` matches, so a derived namespace always satisfies the declared regex. `type`: no default exists anywhere (declaration, door, primitive), so refusing a typeless manifest is the door's own answer (class 1b in package-api.zod.ts's residual table) and Prime Directive #12 forbids inventing one in a consumer. Ordering against the ADR-0087 D1 handshake: the parse now runs before `assertProtocolCompat`, shape before semantics; a manifest both off-spec and protocol-incompatible answers 400 rather than `ProtocolIncompatibleError`, and the handshake fixtures gained `name` / `type` so they still reach the handshake. The parse result is not written back (`declaredManifest.data` unused), so `scope` / `defaultDatasource` defaults are not stored — the same gate-not-normaliser discipline the door records, pinned in both new test files.

3. **Every caller is an authoring install — RIGHT.** At this head the primitive has three non-test callers: the door; `duplicatePackage` (protocol.ts 27526–27567: spreads the stored source manifest, overrides `id` / `name` / `namespace`, `delete dupManifest.scope`, and since #24041 rethrows the install's refusal before any item is copied — the swallowing the cloud seat's note 6236742886 read at cloud's older pin is gone at this base); and `importUnmanagedPackage` (27908), whose base is built in package-unmanaged-install.ts from the identity dispositions — `name`, `version`, `type`, `description`, `defaultDatasource`, `dependencies`, `engines`, `engine` copied; `id` / `namespace` / `scope` not; an undeclared key refused upstream — so a built artifact meets no new refusal there. No in-repo caller sends `type: 'application'` outside tests (the only source hit is the SBOM generator, unrelated).

4. **Stored rows hydrate; tolerance at the read only — RIGHT.** `PackageServicePlugin.start` (service-package index.ts 673–790) runs the D1 handshake and then `registry.installPackage(convertForward(rec.manifest), 'authored')`; nothing there judges `type` / `scope`, and the diff changes only a comment at that seam. The real-stack pin (ObjectKernel + ObjectQLPlugin + SqlDriver on better-sqlite3 + PackageServicePlugin + the real protocol) publishes a `type: 'application'`, `scope: 'environment'` row through the service's own `publish`, restarts, and reads it back as stored with no error line; then a fresh install of the same manifest and a `duplicatePackage` of the stored app are both refused 400 with nothing written to the registry or `sys_packages`. No tolerance was added at any write.

5. **Refusal pins carry status AND code — RIGHT.** protocol.install-manifest-declaration.test.ts pins `resolveThrownHttpError(err)` to `{ status: 400, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' }` (the real boundary resolver), the key path, the verbatim `packageInstallScopeRefusal('cloud')` sentence, the id leg answering first, and zero writer calls. The service-package pins and the flipped pin assert `err.statusCode === 400` and `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(err.statusCode) === 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` — the code leg there is derived from the status rather than read off the throw; acceptable because the throw carries no `.code` and the resolver's answer is pinned once in metadata-protocol, and both halves pin the absence of both writes.

6. **No fixture relaxes a rule — RIGHT.** All 15 fixture files (7 in metadata-protocol, 8 in objectql) add `type: 'app'` (plus `name` where absent) or respell `application` → `app`; no schema, default or gate is loosened. The `scope: 'environment'` left on protocol-package-lifecycle.test.ts's duplicate source is stripped by `duplicatePackage` itself before the write. The flipped pin in hydration-convert-forward.test.ts changes which gate refuses the assembled HotCRM body (400 at the declaration's strict close, not 422 `MisplacedDefaultPageError` at the registry) and keeps asserting that nothing is written; the registry's page refusal keeps its pins in that file's hydration half (`expectMisplacedDefault`, lines 236 and 251) and in objectql's registry-default-record-page.test.ts, so no assertion is lost.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/24086-install-primitive-parses-manifest.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, a bang title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a BREAKING paragraph with FROM → TO and the one-line fix, and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — a category the gate carries (check-adr-0087-registration.mjs); Check Changeset and Lint & Repo Gates are green on this head.
- **Level RIGHT.** A `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; the launch-window guard (check-changeset-no-major.mjs) ships breaking changes as `minor` and refuses `major`, so `minor` is the only admissible level.
- **Package list RIGHT.** The only behavioural source change is metadata-protocol's. service-package's src change is a nine-line comment; objectql's changes are tests only. One package in the frontmatter matches what the diff publishes.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` RIGHT.** No public export is added, removed or changed (metadata-protocol's index, `packages/spec` and `packages/runtime` are untouched; the only new line outside tests is an import); no accept set widens anywhere — the hydration seam's tolerance is behaviour that existed before, now stated, not a new admission; the vitest alias is test infrastructure. The disposition's claim that stored `sys_packages` rows are untouched and keep hydrating is what the real-stack pin measures.

Not a second rule or a second vocabulary.

- q1 (typeless manifest: refuse, or default `type` at the primitive) — **A, refuse**: the declaration has no default, the door refuses, Prime Directive #12 forbids a consumer-side default.
- q2 (`duplicatePackage` of a pre-change base is refused; migrate stored rows?) — **A**: declared is enforced at every write, B is consumer-side tolerance (#12), C is the silent rewrite the disposition refuses. The refusal is reported, not swallowed (#24041, verified at this head) and pinned in the addendum. Row repair belongs to the producer: cloud#2948 / cloud PR #2978 and the cloud maintainer's decision box 6236726201 — outside this repo; **escalated to the adopting seat only as the cloud-pin constraint below**.
